strategies.name: mean_reversion_scalp
strategies.setup: Mean reversion scalps occur after price stretches too far too fast. You are stepping in when emotion peaks and order flow begins to shift. That shift is visible in the tape before it's obvious on the chart.

entry_sequence.action: it's a stock that has a significant price range, is doing high volume, and often trading on a news catalyst or interesting technical pattern

Scalping thrives on liquidity and volatility. You need both. Random tickers with average volume and no catalyst do not provide clean intraday imbalances. They provide choppiness and will inevitably lead to paper cut losses.

I want a very well-defined intraday support or resistance level. Ideally, one that aligns on multiple time frames. Something other participants clearly see as well. Ultimately, the tighter the level, the more defined your risk

You need to be paying attention to how thick or thin the bids and offers are, and look for disparity as well as which side is being more aggressive. Is the offer being taken, or are the bids being smashed? The time and sales window reveals who is being more aggressive. If you are not watching the tape, which is the level two box of the buyers and sellers and the time and sales window, you are missing the story.

On a sharp down move into support, you will often see a moment where volume stalls, and it's this pause where people stop hitting the bid. That pause is often the hesitation of sellers to push their hand and signifies a turn of momentum. As a scalper, you then take the offer and get long in front of that support level

confluences.description: Often, these mean reversion scalps work best when the stock quickly and sharply shoots down to a support level with some massive bids or quickly and sharply shoots up to a resistance level with large offers. The sharper and bigger the move into really big bids or offers, the better it is to scalp a reversal.
Often, all you need is a few high-quality opportunities where structure and order flow align.

stop.description: using the bids as at the support as your protection

targets.description: seeking to capture the bounce we get off that level

variants.name: short_mirror_at_resistance
variants.description: quickly and sharply shoots up to a resistance level with large offers

instrument_classification.notes: Order-flow / tape-reading scalp on in-play cash equities; speaker references share-based examples ($25 / $50 levels, 5,000 shares, Facebook IPO). Strategy mechanic (support/resistance mean-reversion via level-2 and time-and-sales), not an options-mechanic (no Greeks/strikes).

coaching_notes: You are stepping in when emotion peaks and order flow begins to shift.
identify a key emotional level, confirm with the tape, and execute without hesitation
There is no room for distraction, and you're interpreting real-time information and making fast, calculated decisions.
The strategy is also cognitively demanding, requiring sustained focus over the course of a long day.
The margin for error is thin, and a single large mistake can erase many small gains.
Scalping is highly execution-dependent. Minor slippage, hesitation, or routing inefficiencies can eliminate or impair your expected value.
Transaction costs matter significantly because profit targets are small relative to frequency.
The more size you do, the more slippage you face, and in turn the more your edge degrades.
you tend to need to be glued to the desk during market hours
When you get the reps, you'll develop small positive edges, which, when repeated consistently, can compound meaningfully over time.
You do not need too many trades per day... often you can fall for the trap of not being selective enough and your win rate suffers.
